title: Windows Terminal as Keyboard Manager shortcut does not get focus properly
author: tianon

status.label: Actionable fix candidate
status.detail: Current reproduction and source control flow identify a concrete missing new-process focus path.

next_action.label: Design fix

judgment.rationale: Current reproduction and source control flow identify a concrete missing new-process focus path.
evidence: Notepad reproduces independently of Windows Terminal.
The existing-process branch invokes ShowProgram while the new-process branch does not.
judgment.recommended_action: Design a bounded new-process window discovery and foreground-transfer flow with explicit launch semantics.

fix_assessment.rationale: No merged fix references the canonical issue; a duplicate remains closed in favor of this thread.

issue_context.summary: Applications launched by Keyboard Manager shortcut remaps frequently open behind the current foreground window instead of receiving focus.
known_information: The issue reproduces with Windows Terminal and Notepad on PowerToys 0.100.2.
The new process receives focus when the desktop is foreground, but not when Keyboard Manager or another window is foreground.
ForegroundLockTimeout=0 mitigates the problem, confirming Windows foreground-activation policy is involved.
inferences: Keyboard Manager launches the process but does not complete a foreground-transfer protocol permitted by Windows, leaving the new window flashing for attention.
issue_context.analysis: Current CreateOrShowProcessForShortcut calls ShowProgram for an already-running process, but the corresponding call for a newly created process remains commented out. A robust fix must handle delayed top-level window creation and Windows foreground restrictions rather than only call SetForegroundWindow once.
initial_investigation: src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp leaves ShowProgram(processId, ...) commented after new-process creation.
Issue 44720 was closed as a duplicate of this issue; enhancement 39737 separately requests an explicit focused launch mode.

proposed_fixes.title: Transfer foreground activation to newly launched shortcut apps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager starts the target process but omits the ShowProgram/focus path used for existing processes, and therefore relies on default Windows activation that is often denied to the hook-driven launcher.
plan: Add an explicit launch-focus option or make normal visible launches request focus consistently.
Wait with a short bound for the target process's eligible top-level window, then use the established foreground-transfer helper from an allowed UI context.
Handle packaged/multi-process apps, no-window processes, elevation boundaries, and Start another without blocking the keyboard hook.
verification: Launch Notepad and Windows Terminal from a shortcut while Settings, Explorer, and another app are foreground; verify the target receives focus without changing ForegroundLockTimeout.

confidence.rationale: The missing new-process call and foreground-dependent reproduction are strong evidence, though Windows focus restrictions require validating the exact transfer mechanism.
